title: Septic Service Estimate Worksheet
subtitle: Residential Septic Service: prices observed scope, options, and exclusions.
description: Septic Service Estimate Worksheet covers tank, inlet, outlet, baffle, pump, alarm, distribution component, and disposal area. The septic service coordinator records Residential Septic Service observed scope, costs, options, and terms. Septic Service Estimate Worksheet keeps Residential Septic Service exceptions visible until the septic service coordinator handoff.
use_case: Use Septic Service Estimate Worksheet at property, tank access, pump chamber, distribution area, and protected ground surface. Document tank, inlet, outlet, baffle, pump, alarm, distribution component, and disposal area identity before Residential Septic Service begins. Compare tank, inlet, outlet, baffle, pump, alarm, distribution component, and disposal area findings with stated Residential Septic Service criteria; route unresolved Residential Septic Service issues to qualified septic-system reviewer. For Septic Service Estimate Worksheet, confirm requirements for Residential Septic Service. Ask qualified septic-system reviewer to review Residential Septic Service conditions beyond the septic service coordinator's role.

sections.title: Property estimate review and customer identity
sections.guidance: Identify the customer, asset or property, estimator, and basis date before pricing the work.

blocks.label: Residential Septic Service identity

fields.label: System type, tank or component identifier, and access point
Occupancy, last service, symptom, and weather history

blocks.guidance: Use the Residential Septic Service identifier printed on tank, inlet, outlet, baffle, pump, alarm, distribution component, and disposal area or its linked source record.

sections.title: Pricing options and customer decision inputs
sections.guidance: Price the observable work and options. Keep concealed conditions and unconfirmed quantities out of fixed scope.

blocks.label: Residential Septic Service scope observations
items: Access cover, riser, seal, and surface condition
Liquid level, scum, sludge, inlet, outlet, and baffle observation
Pump, float, alarm, control, and electrical indication
Backup, odor, surfacing effluent, and wet-area evidence
Vehicle, excavation, fall, biological, and confined-space boundary
Post-service level, closure, alarm, and flow observation
blocks.guidance: Mark what was observed or supplied as estimate input; explain anything material that could not be inspected.

sections.title: Estimate exception and change conditions
sections.guidance: State what could change the price, timing, method, or scope before the customer or responsible party decides.

blocks.label: Do not proceed without control
blocks.guidance: Stop normal processing when access safety, containment, backup, structural integrity, disposal, or qualified escalation remains unresolved. Protect tank, inlet, outlet, baffle, pump, alarm, distribution component, and disposal area; document the Residential Septic Service notification and await qualified septic-system reviewer direction.

blocks.label: Conditions that may require a revised estimate or specialist review
items: Unsafe opening, fall, biological, or confined-space exposure
Backup or surfacing effluent threatens occupancy
Damaged tank or component requires excavation
Electrical, structural, or regulatory work outside scope
blocks.guidance: For Residential Septic Service, identify affected tank, inlet, outlet, baffle, pump, alarm, distribution component, and disposal area scope; ask septic service coordinator to document the Residential Septic Service immediate control before continuing.
